commit_scope: Restore the Hati grocery balance from its connected Sheet, resolve production-shaped legacy presence identities, and keep large substrate recipes deployable on PostgreSQL.
evidence_refs: The merged deployment installed SHA 61070d093bcc5614ad95e3029b58d190bd500f4b, but /people/urs-muff/edit still rendered the soft-404 page.
The source-backed Urs graph record declares legacy_ids containing urs-muff; the first resolver implementation queried aliases only.
The failed Hostinger rollout log showed PostgreSQL rejecting a 10877-character recipe value because uq_substrate_serialized exceeded the btree index-row limit.

The Google Sheets connector verified the configured Hati Suci - Food workbook, its Sheet1 summary formulas, and a current calculated balance without reading or recording household transaction rows in this receipt.
The app contract was write-only: it mirrored graph entries into Sheets but calculated remaining balance solely from graph rows, excluding the pre-app ledger history.
The first repair read the anonymous CSV export and trusted sheet_synced as an atomic boundary; exact-head review exposed both the privacy leak and the append/flag crash race before merge.

The repaired carrier authenticates every request, returns only Sisa plus matches among caller-supplied pending entry IDs, and makes appends idempotent with an Entry ID column; the spreadsheet can remain private.

New graph writes carry the entry-id-v1 protocol marker; unmarked unsynced legacy rows remain explicitly unknown, make balance unavailable, and are excluded from automatic replay or deletion until migrated.

Historical-baseline availability and the signed pending fold now execute in endpoint_grocery_remaining.fk; an unavailable Sheet produces an explicit unavailable balance rather than an incomplete graph-only number.

Deletion uses one Apps Script lock to serialize original appends, a private durable cancellation marker, and the stable reversal; it preserves the graph row on uncertainty and physically removes it only after the atomic carrier receipt.

The graph service excludes grocery_spend by default from node, edge, traversal, stats, and proof reads, so generic graph routes, flow rendering, edge/entity APIs, public profiles, and future generic consumers cannot expose the private cells or their connected edges; dedicated grocery reconciliation alone uses its purpose-built raw snapshot.

Single-node reads now inherit the same private default, the authenticated grocery carrier names its unfiltered lookup explicitly, and zoom roots, descendants, edges, and question mutations prune grocery cells before rendering or mutation.

ID-based edge patch and deletion now apply the same private endpoint predicate inside graph_service, so both public edge routers preserve relations connected to grocery cells even when an edge ID is known.
The concepts edge fallback now reuses graph_service.get_edges instead of querying Edge directly, preserving the same private-endpoint predicate when a concept has no public neighbors.
A conflicting generic node create now raises a sanitized dedicated-private ownership error instead of returning the existing grocery row from the database integrity-conflict branch.

Meeting capture now rejects dedicated-private IDs before updating an existing meeting or participant and before creating a concept relation, preventing unauthenticated upsert conflicts from reading or changing grocery cells.

Contribution listing, contribution lookup, and inventory-flow aggregation now read edges through graph_service.list_edges, preventing raw contribution queries from exposing relations connected to grocery cells.

Graph-service node updates, node deletion, ordinary edge creation, strict edge creation, and provenance-edge creation now reject dedicated-private endpoints by default; the authenticated grocery carrier opts in explicitly only for its own reconciliation writes.
Contribution detail lookup now uses one exact JSON-property query with the shared private-edge predicate, preserving privacy and no-row-ceiling behavior without an OFFSET race.

Graph-service node creation now also defaults to denying dedicated-private types; the authenticated grocery writer and explicit reconciliation fixtures are the only callers that name private-create intent.
Meeting resonance recall now drops any item whose participant, concept, or concept-part node resolves to a dedicated-private type, so forged public capture metadata cannot serialize a grocery row.
The meeting-recall private-stub decision lives in a focused helper, restoring the maintainability audit to its 112-long-function baseline after exact-head CI detected a one-function regression.

The Apps Script summary returns both acknowledged and cancelled subsets under the same lock; a deletion completed after the database snapshot therefore cannot leave a stale pending amount in the returned balance.

Restructure persists the exact ledger tab's immutable Sheet ID; the carrier resolves only that ID thereafter, while a legacy unbound workbook may self-bind only when exactly one tab has the restructured ledger shape. Missing or ambiguous identity fails closed before any write is acknowledged.

The developer quick-start timing witness explicitly loads the required pytest-asyncio plugin, disables unrelated host plugin autoload and assertion rewriting, and gates on child user-CPU time while retaining system and wall time in failures; its 120-second safety ceiling permits heavily stalled hosts to reach that measurement without weakening the ten-second work budget.
The documented Sheet restructure preserves existing Entry IDs across re-runs instead of erasing the idempotency ledger.
The restructure now holds the same Apps Script lock for its full snapshot-and-rewrite interval, excluding concurrent append and delete operations.

Grocery reconciliation reads every row with one immutable-ID-ordered database statement before declaring the legacy-unknown set empty; a 2,001-row focused witness proves there is no page ceiling or mutable OFFSET seam.
Graph identity lookup now recognizes both aliases and legacy_ids with indexed JSON containment and exact membership confirmation.
PostgreSQL substrate uniqueness now uses a bounded md5 expression key while exact full serialized text remains part of every lookup; SQLite retains exact tuple uniqueness.
A PostgreSQL uniqueness-migration failure now clears the cached engine and raises through startup, guaranteeing the supervisor retries the complete schema gate instead of serving the old constraint.
PostgreSQL startup reads durable catalog state and skips both locking DDL statements once the legacy constraint is absent and the digest index exists.
The outer lifespan database-table gate now propagates schema failures instead of logging and continuing startup.

The first exact-head Linux run exposed a preserved graph-service source contract: count_nodes must keep the public one-argument signature. Privacy is now unconditional inside that service method, leaving no caller-controlled bypass.
No private profile content is included in this receipt.

local_validation.summary: After rebasing all eleven repair commits onto origin/main at 8aed234c2, every structural guard and 406 functional API tests passed. The flow child passes all 13 tests; its performance witness enforces the ten-second user-CPU budget instead of variable host wall time, including a focused pass that took 48.41 seconds wall on the saturated host. The documented carrier compiles as JavaScript and a focused contract proves it persists and resolves the immutable restructured-tab identity rather than tab order. All 73 focused graph-port, grocery reconciliation, privacy, graph-layer, meeting-capture, and contribution tests pass, including the exact-head review cases for single-node, zoom, conflict, raw-upsert, raw-edge, and unbounded filtered detail reads. The authenticated Apps Script carrier is saved in the live project without its persistent secret or deployment yet; no household transaction rows or exact balance were read.

ci_validation.summary: The exact-head Linux run passed evidence, drift, maintainability, native Form proof, and 2,193 functional API tests, then failed only because the developer-speed meta-test measured 10.8 seconds of shared-runner wall time. That witness now preserves the ten-second work budget as child user-CPU time and reports system/wall time diagnostically. Exact-head review then found that tab-order selection could redirect the carrier; immutable tab binding with fail-closed legacy discovery and focused proof repairs that stability gap. Fresh exact-head CI will run after this repair is pushed.
